vectors.name: a_persons_event
vectors.why: An ID commits to a key and a recovery rule. Nothing says what it's an ID of.

vectors.name: an_agents_event
vectors.why: An agent's is the same kind, with no owner in it.

vectors.name: another_event
vectors.why: Another key gives another ID.

vectors.name: trailing_space
vectors.why: Padding would let a sender grow every message it sends.

vectors.name: leading_space
vectors.why: Same.

vectors.name: trailing_newline
vectors.why: Same.

vectors.name: space_in_json
vectors.why: One key must have one ID.

vectors.name: escaped_character
vectors.why: An escape is another encoding of the same event.

vectors.name: reordered_fields
vectors.why: A different field order is another encoding.

vectors.name: reordered_rule
vectors.why: So is one inside the rule.

vectors.name: respelled_key
vectors.why: A base64 character with different spare bits decodes to the same key.

vectors.name: unknown_field
vectors.why: Unknown fields are refused.

vectors.name: duplicate_field
vectors.why: Parsers disagree on which duplicate wins, so duplicates are refused.

vectors.name: alg_none
vectors.why: The event can't choose another algorithm.

vectors.name: version_3
vectors.why: An unknown version is refused, not guessed at.

vectors.name: event_with_no_sealing_key
vectors.why: Without one nothing could be sealed to this ID, and one added later would be a new ID.

vectors.name: sealing_key_is_the_signing_key
vectors.why: One key never does both jobs.

vectors.name: sealing_key_off_the_curve
vectors.why: Nothing could be sealed to it.

vectors.name: event_naming_a_role
vectors.why: There's one kind of ID, so there's no role.

vectors.name: event_naming_an_owner
vectors.why: Who an agent acts for is a separate statement, or it couldn't change.

vectors.name: event_with_no_recovery_rule
vectors.why: A rule can't be added later without a new ID.

vectors.name: not_json
vectors.why: Garbage is refused without a crash.

vectors.name: short_key
vectors.why: A key must be a 65-byte uncompressed point.

vectors.name: compressed_key
vectors.why: Only the uncompressed form is valid.

vectors.name: wrong_point_tag
vectors.why: The first byte must be 4.

vectors.name: unknown_rule
vectors.why: A rule nobody here can check can't be followed.

vectors.name: commitment_not_a_hash
vectors.why: The commitment is 64 hex characters.

vectors.name: commitment_uppercase
vectors.why: One rule has one spelling.

vectors.name: backup_is_the_key
vectors.why: Stealing the key would be stealing the backup too.

vectors.name: a_passkey_owners_event
vectors.why: An owner's key can be a passkey, tied to the RP ID it was made for.

vectors.name: passkey_event_with_no_rp
vectors.why: A passkey signs for one RP ID, which its ID names.

vectors.name: file_key_event_with_an_rp
vectors.why: A file key has none.

vectors.name: passkey_event_as_version_4
vectors.why: The version, the algorithm and the RP ID agree, or the event is refused.

vectors.name: passkey_rp_with_es256
vectors.why: Same.

vectors.name: passkey_rp_after_the_sealing_key
vectors.why: One event has one order.

vectors.name: passkey_rp_with_a_port
vectors.why: An RP ID is a hostname alone.

vectors.name: passkey_rp_in_capitals
vectors.why: In its one spelling.

vectors.name: passkey_rp_with_a_trailing_dot
vectors.why: Same.

vectors.name: passkey_rp_an_ip_address
vectors.why: WebAuthn takes no IP address as an RP ID.

vectors.name: passkey_rp_localhost
vectors.why: Any program on the owner's machine can serve a page at localhost, on any port, and have their touch sign what it likes.

vectors.name: passkey_rp_under_localhost
vectors.why: A name under localhost reaches only this machine too.

vectors.name: backup_key_matches
vectors.why: An untested backup isn't recovery, so setup proves the file matches the commitment.

vectors.name: wrong_backup_key
vectors.why: Another key doesn't match.

vectors.name: recovered_id
vectors.why: The ID doesn't change, and the new key counts.

vectors.name: recovered_twice
vectors.why: The next rule's backup takes over.

vectors.name: event_alone
vectors.why: An ID nobody recovered is just its event.

vectors.name: recovered_by_a_stolen_key
vectors.why: A thief holding the key can't name the next one.

vectors.name: recovered_by_a_strangers_backup
vectors.why: Nor can anyone with a key of their own.

vectors.name: naming_the_backup_and_signed_by_another
vectors.why: Naming the real backup isn't signing with it.

vectors.name: the_used_backup_again
vectors.why: A backup works once.

vectors.name: a_statement_for_another_id
vectors.why: A statement fits one ID.

vectors.name: a_statement_out_of_order
vectors.why: And one place in its history.

vectors.name: the_same_statement_twice
vectors.why: Which it can't take twice.

vectors.name: the_same_rule_again
vectors.why: A recovery names a new backup, since this one has been shown.

vectors.name: the_new_key_is_the_new_backup
vectors.why: The same goes for the key and backup after a recovery.

vectors.name: a_new_key_keeping_the_old_sealing_key
vectors.why: A key replaced because it was stolen went with the sealing key beside it, so a thief could still read what's sealed to it.

vectors.name: a_sealing_key_on_its_own_curve_point_is_the_signing_key
vectors.why: One key never does both jobs, after a recovery too.

vectors.name: wrong_statement_type
vectors.why: Rules signatures can't pass as recoveries.

vectors.name: recovered_to_a_passkey
vectors.why: An owner with a file key moves to a passkey with a version 3, which names it and its RP ID.

vectors.name: recovered_from_a_passkey_to_a_file_key
vectors.why: And back with a version 2. The backup is a plain key either way.

vectors.name: version_2_recovery_naming_an_rp
vectors.why: A version 2 names a file key, and has one spelling.

vectors.name: version_3_recovery_with_no_rp
vectors.why: A passkey signs for one RP ID, which the recovery names.

vectors.name: version_3_recovery_with_another_alg
vectors.why: A version 3 names a passkey, whose alg is webauthn-es256 and nothing else.

vectors.name: recovery_keeping_the_key_as_a_passkey
vectors.why: One point is one key, held one way.

vectors.name: a_reader_learns_of_a_recovery
vectors.why: The longer history counts.

vectors.name: an_older_copy_changes_nothing
vectors.why: A host can't bring a stolen key back by showing an old copy.

vectors.name: the_signature_respelled
vectors.why: An ES256 signature has a second valid spelling, which anyone can work out.

vectors.name: a_respelled_signature_isnt_a_second_recovery
vectors.why: Or a host could make one real recovery look like two, and a reader refuse the real one.

vectors.name: two_recoveries_are_refused
vectors.why: Only the backup can make two, and nothing here can say which is real.

vectors.name: binding
vectors.why: The owner and the agent both say this agent acts for this owner, at this address.

vectors.name: binding_by_the_agent_key
vectors.why: A stolen agent key can't sign the owner's half.

vectors.name: binding_for_another_address
vectors.why: A host can't reuse Ana's binding at another address.

vectors.name: binding_at_another_host
vectors.why: Or at another host.

vectors.name: mallory_claims_anas_agent
vectors.why: Mallory can sign that it's hers, and the agent never agreed.

vectors.name: binding_with_another_bindings_acceptance
vectors.why: An agent's yes covers one exact statement.

vectors.name: binding_with_no_acceptance
vectors.why: Both halves have to be there.

vectors.name: binding_with_no_vouch
vectors.why: The agent's backup has to vouch for the owner, or a stolen agent key could name one.

vectors.name: binding_vouched_by_another_backup
vectors.why: Only a backup the agent's ID committed to can vouch.

vectors.name: binding_vouched_by_the_agent_key
vectors.why: The agent's own key isn't its backup.

vectors.name: binding_vouching_for_another_owner
vectors.why: A vouch names one owner.

vectors.name: binding_vouching_for_other_keys
vectors.why: A vouch names the agent's keys when its ID committed to that backup.

vectors.name: binding_for_a_copy_moved_onto_other_keys
vectors.why: What the owner's backup vouched for counts only for the keys it named, so a copy moved to it onto others gets nothing.

vectors.name: binding_for_a_sibling
vectors.why: An owner's other agent can't use this one's binding, or a stolen key could claim its handle.

vectors.name: binding_naming_another_owner
vectors.why: The signature is good, and the document names someone else.

vectors.name: binding_with_wrong_typ
vectors.why: Rules signatures can't pass as bindings.

vectors.name: binding_from_before_the_owners_recovery
vectors.why: What the old key signed stops counting, or a thief's would go on counting.

vectors.name: binding_by_a_passkey
vectors.why: The challenge is the hash of the exact header and payload, so the passkey signed this binding.

vectors.name: binding_by_a_passkey_with_more_client_data
vectors.why: Browsers add fields of their own to clientDataJSON, and those are allowed.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_with_another_challenge
vectors.why: A passkey's yes to something else isn't a yes to this.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_from_another_origin
vectors.why: A page elsewhere can't have made it.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_from_another_port
vectors.why: Nor one on another port of the same host.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_from_a_subdomain
vectors.why: Nor one on a subdomain, which a browser lets use the RP ID.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_for_another_rp
vectors.why: The passkey was made for this RP ID, and no other.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_with_nobody_present
vectors.why: Nobody touched the authenticator.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_with_nobody_verified
vectors.why: Nobody showed a fingerprint, face or PIN, which every passkey store asks for.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_made_while_making_a_passkey
vectors.why: Only an assertion signs, never a passkey being made.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_in_another_sites_frame
vectors.why: A page framed by another site can't have made it.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_with_no_challenge
vectors.why: What a reader checks has to be there.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_with_a_key_twice
vectors.why: Parsers disagree on which of two keys wins.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_past_2_kib
vectors.why: A signature segment is at most 2048 characters.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_with_client_data_after_a_bom
vectors.why: JSON starts with its first value, so a byte-order mark before it is refused, as some decoders would silently drop it.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_with_a_lone_surrogate_in_a_key
vectors.why: An escape for half a character is no text at all, even in a key a reader skips, or two readers could disagree on what's valid.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_with_a_lone_surrogate_in_a_value
vectors.why: The same in a value a reader skips.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_with_client_data_not_utf8
vectors.why: JSON is UTF-8, even in a field a reader skips, or two readers could disagree on what's valid.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_with_authenticator_data_missing_a_counter_byte
vectors.why: authenticatorData has a 4-byte counter after its RP hash and flags, even though it's ignored.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_with_authenticator_data_too_short_for_an_rp_hash
vectors.why: Too short to hold the RP hash at all.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_by_another_passkey
vectors.why: Only this ID's passkey counts.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_from_a_plain_http_page
vectors.why: A passkey's page is https:// and its RP ID, never plain HTTP.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_for_a_host_from_a_localhost_page
vectors.why: A page at http://localhost, which any program on the owner's machine can serve, never signs for a host's name.

vectors.name: binding_by_a_localhost_passkey_on_a_port
vectors.why: Its owner ID is refused, as is all it signs, from the page that made it.

vectors.name: binding_by_a_localhost_passkey_over_https
vectors.why: Or from https://localhost, which is no safer.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_with_a_signature_in_loose_der
vectors.why: The signature is strict DER, so it has one spelling: a needless zero before a number is refused, though the numbers are the same.

vectors.name: binding_by_a_passkey_in_a_batch
vectors.why: One touch signed this binding and the rules with it: the challenge hashes the list, which holds this binding's own hash once.

vectors.name: rules_by_a_passkey_in_the_same_batch
vectors.why: The rules from the same touch verify alone, by the same segment. A reader of either learns only the other's hash.

vectors.name: passkey_batch_without_its_own_hash
vectors.why: A touch over a list that doesn't hold this object's hash signed something else.

vectors.name: passkey_batch_listing_its_hash_twice
vectors.why: Each hash is listed once, so a list has one meaning.

vectors.name: passkey_batch_of_nine
vectors.why: A batch is at most 8 objects.

vectors.name: passkey_batch_of_one
vectors.why: One object alone is signed without a list.

vectors.name: passkey_batch_in_capitals
vectors.why: A hash has one spelling, lowercase hex.

vectors.name: passkey_batch_reordered
vectors.why: The challenge hashes the list in its order, so the same touch with the list reordered is refused.

vectors.name: passkey_binding_signed_as_a_file_key
vectors.why: An ID whose key is a passkey takes only WA256, even from the same point.

vectors.name: binding_by_a_file_key_signed_as_a_passkey
vectors.why: And an ID whose key is a file key takes only ES256.

vectors.name: binding_for_an_agent_whose_key_is_a_passkey
vectors.why: Only an owner's key may be a passkey.

vectors.name: transfer
vectors.why: The agent moves to the owner the old one named, with its ID unchanged.

vectors.name: the_same_owner_again
vectors.why: An owner can sign a newer one for themselves.

vectors.name: the_same_owner_going_back
vectors.why: But not bring back an older one.

vectors.name: a_new_owner_with_no_release
vectors.why: A stolen agent key and an owner of its own don't move an agent.

vectors.name: a_release_to_someone_else
vectors.why: It names one new owner.

vectors.name: a_revocation_isnt_a_transfer
vectors.why: A release naming nobody moves it to nobody.

vectors.name: a_release_by_someone_else
vectors.why: Only the current owner can give it up.

vectors.name: a_release_for_another_agent
vectors.why: It covers one agent.

vectors.name: a_release_older_than_the_binding
vectors.why: The owner has signed since, so what they released then says nothing now.

vectors.name: a_binding_older_than_its_release
vectors.why: The new owner's statement comes after.

vectors.name: revocation
vectors.why: With nobody named, the agent acts for nobody until its owner signs again.

vectors.name: release_to_a_new_owner
vectors.why: It can name who's next.

vectors.name: revocation_by_the_agent_key
vectors.why: An agent can't release itself.

vectors.name: release_for_another_agent
vectors.why: A release covers one agent.

vectors.name: registration
vectors.why: The proof covers the body, which holds the binding.

vectors.name: registration_by_whoever_holds_the_code
vectors.why: A binding and the code are all it takes, so the next case is refused for its MAC alone.

vectors.name: captured_signup_mac_with_another_owners_binding
vectors.why: What's read on the wire can't take the handle for someone else.

vectors.name: signup_made_with_another_code
vectors.why: A MAC only fits the code it was made with.

vectors.name: captured_proof_with_another_binding
vectors.why: Issue 7: a captured proof can't claim another handle.

vectors.name: captured_proof_with_another_code
vectors.why: Or spend another signup code.

vectors.name: binding_for_another_host
vectors.why: A binding for elsewhere can't register here, even when the proof fits.

vectors.name: retirement
vectors.why: The owner's signed stop signal for a stolen agent key.

vectors.name: retirement_by_the_agent_key
vectors.why: An agent can't retire itself or a sibling.
